newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda says to boost car production.
newsitem.headline: Mazda says to boost car production.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp said on Tuesday it would boost output at one of its two car plants in Japan to meet increasing demand from Europe.

The car maker plans to raise the operation rate at its Hofu plant in western Japan to an average 50 percent of capacity in the period to September 30, 1997 and to an average 60 percent during the six months to March 31, 1998, Mazda said.
Operation rates at the Hofu plant, capable of producing 390,000 cars a year, have averaged 40 percent in recent years, a Mazda spokesman said.
"The planned increase is to cope with increasing demand in the European market," the spokesman said.

Mazda's other car assembly plant at its headquarters in Hiroshima, western Japan, is currently operating at almost full capacity, the spokesman said. The Hiroshima plant can produce 710,000 cars a year.
Plans for operation rates after April 1998 were not available.
